Welcome to the course on Stability Analysis for Multi-Environment Trials (METs)!

This is comprehensive guide to understanding and implementing techniques for assessing Genotype \(\times\) Environment (G\(\times\)E) interaction.

Package installation

To install the metan package from github, you will need to have the package pak installed first. If you are a windows user, it is also suggested to install R Tools to compile the package binaries.

Code 
if (!requireNamespace("pak", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("pak")
}
# Now install metan from GitHub using pak
pak::pak("nepem-ufsc/metan")
ℹ Loading metadata database

Topics Covered

1. Data Preparation and ANOVA-Based Analysis

  • Setup and Data Management (R): Loading necessary packages (metan, tidyverse), importing sample MET datasets, conducting data quality checks, and visualizing raw means.
  • ANOVA for METs: Executing ANOVA models (individual and joint) to partition Genotype (G), Environment (E), and G\(\times\)E effects.
  • ANOVA-derived Stability Indexes: Calculating traditional indexes, Plaisted & Peterson (1959), and Wricke’s Ecovalence.

2. Univariate Stability Methods Implementation

  • Regression-based Stability Indexes: Fitting Finlay & Wilkinson regression models and calculating the Environmental Index (EI).
  • Factorial Regression: Incorporating explicit environmental covariates (e.g., thermal, hydrological, radiation) into the model using PCA and forward-stepwise selection.
  • Lin & Binns Superiority Index: Calculating the \(P_i\) index (Loss Function) to identify stable and superior genotypes under different environmental conditions.

3. Multivariate and Simultaneous Selection

  • AMMI Analysis: Fitting Additive Main Effects and Multiplicative Interaction models and generating AMMI1 and AMMI2 biplots.
  • GGE Biplots Analysis: Using GGE biplots for assessing mean performance vs. stability, which-won-where patterns, and test environment evaluation.
  • Simultaneous Selection: Implementing WAASB (Weighted Average of Absolute Scores) and WAASBY (balancing yield and stability) indices.

Welcome to the course on **Stability Analysis for Multi-Environment Trials (METs)**!

This is comprehensive guide to understanding and implementing techniques for assessing Genotype $\times$ Environment (G$\times$E) interaction.

## Package installation
To install the `metan` package from github, you will need to have the package `pak` installed first. If you are a windows user, it is also suggested to install [R Tools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/) to compile the package binaries.

```{r}
if (!requireNamespace("pak", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("pak")
}
# Now install metan from GitHub using pak
pak::pak("nepem-ufsc/metan")
```



## Topics Covered

### 1. Data Preparation and ANOVA-Based Analysis
- **Setup and Data Management (R):** Loading necessary packages (`metan`, `tidyverse`), importing sample MET datasets, conducting data quality checks, and visualizing raw means.
- **ANOVA for METs:** Executing ANOVA models (individual and joint) to partition Genotype (G), Environment (E), and G$\times$E effects.
- **ANOVA-derived Stability Indexes:** Calculating traditional indexes, Plaisted & Peterson (1959), and Wricke's Ecovalence.

### 2. Univariate Stability Methods Implementation
- **Regression-based Stability Indexes:** Fitting Finlay & Wilkinson regression models and calculating the Environmental Index (EI).
- **Factorial Regression:** Incorporating explicit environmental covariates (e.g., thermal, hydrological, radiation) into the model using PCA and forward-stepwise selection.
- **Lin & Binns Superiority Index:** Calculating the $P_i$ index (Loss Function) to identify stable and superior genotypes under different environmental conditions.

### 3. Multivariate and Simultaneous Selection
- **AMMI Analysis:** Fitting Additive Main Effects and Multiplicative Interaction models and generating AMMI1 and AMMI2 biplots.
- **GGE Biplots Analysis:** Using GGE biplots for assessing mean performance vs. stability, which-won-where patterns, and test environment evaluation.
- **Simultaneous Selection:** Implementing WAASB (Weighted Average of Absolute Scores) and WAASBY (balancing yield and stability) indices.
